source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The folder API separates setting a numeric junk score/origin/percentage from acting on messages already classified. performActionsOnJunkMsgs can mark read or move/delete without setting the score; its unit test deliberately keeps an empty score during action-only cases. The JS wrapper waits for the junk callback before starting good-message actions and rejects with Error on a failed callback. Empty/no-action branches notify success synchronously. The copy listener forwards later completion, but the selected native CopyMessages/DeleteMessages calls do not store their immediate return in rv, so this inspection does not establish delivery of every failure to the callback. The read-state preference here is the manual-mark preference; automatic-classification preference rules remain separate. Part 1does not remove the view duplicate until a later patch. No test ran.
title: Separate junk-score updates from actions and wait for action callbacks
